name: Leadpages
description: Leadpages is a landing-page, website, pop-up, form, lead-capture, integration, webhook, and marketing-automation platform for converting visitors into leads and customers.
agentUseSummary: Leadpages now advertises programmatic API keys, but its public documentation does not yet publish the API authority, authentication header, endpoint schemas, permissions, pagination, response fields, rate limits, or error contract required for a safe Relay wrapper. Relay therefore collects no key and mounts no page, form, lead, automation, webhook, integration, or mutation tools pending provider review.

blocked.label: Read lead or submission data
blocked.description: Leads, form submissions, identities, contact fields, consent fields, pages, sites, pop-ups, analytics, and integrations remain unavailable.

blocked.description: Pages, sites, forms, automations, webhooks, integrations, publishing, lead routing, and every mutation remain unavailable.

providerSetup.blocker: Leadpages' May–June 2026 public support documentation confirms account API-key generation but does not publish the API authority, authentication header, endpoints, permissions, paging, response schema, rate limits, error model, or safe read semantics. No authenticated provider console may be opened in this worker task to inspect private documentation.
providerSetup.nextAction: Leadpages publishes or supplies a reviewable current API reference and OpenAPI schema outside the provider console. A follow-up security review then verifies key transport and rotation, chooses a non-sensitive bounded read, implements exact request and response constraints, and tests it in a non-production customer account before Relay enables connection.

evidence.supports: Leadpages' current integration guide documents API-key generation under Account > API Keys and broad native integration, automation and webhook capabilities, but provides no API authority, request, response, permission or error reference.

Leadpages' current account-settings guide confirms that customers can create, view and revoke API keys for custom tools, automation scripts and third-party services without documenting how those keys authenticate or which API operations they authorize.

The official integration knowledge base documents the product's broad lead collection and third-party integration surface but does not expose a current public developer API reference suitable for a pinned runtime wrapper.
